The operator never degrades silently: every guarantee it cannot provide surfaces as a condition on
the Agent (NFR-8). This page is the whole vocabulary — 39 condition types, and the 71 reason
strings the operator can set on them — extracted from the code rather than written beside it.

**How this page is produced.** The condition types, their owned and sticky classification, the
reason strings, and every call site below are read out of `api/v1alpha1` and
`internal/controller` with `go/packages` and `go/types`, by `cmd/refgen`. Three things per reason
are NOT in the code and are written by hand in `internal/refgen/reasons.yaml`: what state produces it, what the operator
does about it, and whether traffic is withdrawn. Those three are held to the code by the generator
— a reason with no entry, or an entry with no reason, fails `make reference` and so fails CI.

**What this page does not claim.** It does not claim a condition and a reason are set together on
every pass that reaches a call site; a pass asserts what it observed. It does not claim the reason
a given pass picks where a call site can set several — those rows say which set. And "referenced by
a test" means a test file names the string, which is weaker than pinning it: nine tests in this
repository once passed with their subject deleted.

**And the join has a limit worth naming.** It pins the SET of reasons — a new one cannot ship
undescribed, and a description cannot outlive its reason. It does NOT prove the three annotated
answers are still true of the code: behaviour can change under a reason whose name does not. What
covers that is weaker and indirect. Each reason's own constant doc comment is reproduced below, so
when the code's comment moves the page moves, `make verify` fails, and a human reads the diff — which is
how the annotation for `AuthPolicyNotAttached` was found stale after design 03 A83 landed. That is a
prompt to look, not a proof, and it has one hole it cannot cover: behaviour that changes while the
reason's constant AND its doc comment both stay put. A83 is that shape minus one edit — it happened
to reword the comment. Nothing on this page would have caught it if it had not.

## Phases

`status.phase` is the one-word summary `kubectl get ag` prints. It is a rollup; the conditions below are the detail.

AgentPhase renders in `kubectl get agents`. Guard states (BudgetHeld, Killed) win over rollout states.

`Pending` · `Held` · `Canary` · `Ready` · `Degraded` · `BudgetHeld` · `Killed`


## Condition types

**Owned** means the reconciler is this condition's sole author, so a pass that does not assert it
CLEARS it — its absence is the signal that it no longer applies. A type that is not owned belongs to
another controller and is carried forward untouched. **Sticky** means it stays in the list once set
and flips to `False` rather than disappearing, because for a normal-true condition like `Ready` an
absence is indistinguishable from "never evaluated". Both are read from `ownedTypes` and
`stickyTypes` in `internal/controller/conditions.go`.

### What each type means

The doc comment attached to each type's declaration in `api/v1alpha1`, verbatim. For the first constant of a group that is sometimes the comment introducing the GROUP rather than that one type — the generator reproduces what is attached and does not re-attribute it.

- **`EnvSourceProtectionUnavailable`** — CondEnvSourceProtectionUnavailable is NO LONGER RAISED. It announced the env-source bypass while A20, A35 and A42 were design; A42's run namespace closed the last of it (design 02 A61) and a real-cluster test proves it. The type stays in §3.1's closed vocabulary so an operator built after A42 can still CLEAR a stale True left by one built before; removing it from the API is a later, separate amendment.
- **`PolicyCompileFailed`** — Thirteen conditions design 02 §3.1 declares that had no constant here. Nine predate the round that added this comment; the vocabulary drifted unnoticed because the closure test asserted a hard-coded count and never compared a single name. Grouped by the design that raises each.
- **`Progressing`** — CondProgressing reports a rollout in flight. Added by A13: without it, a spec edit on a serving agent had to be reported either as Canary — whose meaning §3.3 fixes as "weights are shifting", which is false before design 03 exists — or as Ready=False on an agent that is serving normally, which trips every alert keyed on the canonical condition.
- **`RevisionHashCollision`** — CondRevisionHashCollision reports two DIFFERENT projections sharing one 40-bit revision name (A37). It is terminal: the operator will not adopt or rewrite a workload whose recorded digest disagrees with the desired one, because doing so is exactly the gate bypass the collision buys.
- **`RevisionMaterialCollision`** — CondRevisionMaterialCollision reports a revision-scoped copy that already exists under the expected name but does not satisfy the whole invariant — kind, owner UID, immutability, bytes (A39). It is terminal for the same reason as above: adopting by name is how a name that looks right comes to hold content nobody hashed.
- **`RevisionMaterialUnavailable`** — CondRevisionMaterialUnavailable reports a revision-scoped copy that is missing, or whose owner UID or digest disagrees with the record (A41). The revision's route goes to weight 0: losing availability is the right direction when the alternative is serving material nobody can vouch for.
- **`RevisionRecordUnsupported`** — CondRevisionRecordUnsupported reports a retained revision whose record was written by a schema version this operator no longer carries a decoder for (design 03 A39). Deliberately NOT the corruption condition: "damaged" and "written by a version I dropped" call for different human actions, and collapsing them tells the operator to go looking for the wrong thing.
- **`RunNamespaceUnavailable`** — CondRunNamespaceUnavailable reports that the operator-owned run namespace an Agent's workload and material must live in (design 02 A42/A60) cannot be used. Reasons: NotCreatedByOperator (a namespace of that name exists that the binding record does not vouch for — pre-created, or deleted and recreated), NameCollision (two source namespaces truncate-and-hash to one run name), Terminating (teardown in progress; clears by itself), BindingRecordInvalid (the record is missing a field, carries an unknown state, or a schema version this operator does not decode) and LabelAuthorityAbsent (the admission policies that reserve the assayd.dev namespace labels to the operator are not installed). All but Terminating are terminal until a human acts, and the message says what to do.

## Reasons

One section per reason string the operator can set, in alphabetical order.

### `ActiveRevisionServiceUnaddressable`

**Conditions:** `Degraded=True`, `Ready=False`

**Constant:** none — written as a string literal at the call site.

**Set at:**

- `internal/controller/agent_controller.go:991` in `Reconcile()` — constant at the call site
- `internal/controller/agent_controller.go:989` in `Reconcile()` — constant at the call site

**Referenced by a test:** **no — no test file in this repository names it.** Nothing here fails if it changes or stops being set.

**State:** The active revision is not the desired one, and the active revision's Service exists with no ClusterIP: `spec.clusterIP` is empty (an `ExternalName` Service) or `None` (headless). Nothing that addresses the revision by ClusterIP reaches it, the operator's own card fetch included. Whether the gateway still delivers to it is not established: a headless Service with a selector still has EndpointSlices, and what a gateway does with an `ExternalName` backend is implementation-specific. The usual cause is an owner editing the spec to recover from a broken Service, which moves the desired revision on and leaves the broken one behind.

**What the operator does:** Reads the active revision's Service live and writes nothing to it: sets `Ready=False` and `Degraded=True` with this reason and phase `Degraded`, then carries on to the gateway step. It checks the ClusterIP and nothing else — a wrong selector, ports, `internalTrafficPolicy: Local` or any other shape on that Service is reported by nothing. It does not repair or re-create the object, because it converges only the desired revision. A missing Service, or one it cannot read, raises nothing. A non-transient error from the gateway step later in the same pass replaces this reason on `Ready`, and on `Degraded` for a served Agent. The message's remedy is to revert the spec edit or to wait for the new revision to promote; it never says to delete the Service, which leaves the route naming nothing.

**Traffic:** **not withdrawn** — the route goes on serving; only status changes.

**Code and design disagree:** Design 03 A81 describes `Ready` and `Degraded` reading `ServingRouteNotAccepted` on a pass where the Gateway refuses a served Agent's route. This report sets `Ready=False` before the gateway step and `withholdReady` never overrides a `Ready` that is already False, so on a pass where both fire `Ready` and `Degraded` read this reason while `PolicyApplyIncomplete` reads `ServingRouteNotAccepted` — measured by `TestAnUnaddressableActiveServiceAndARefusedRouteOnOnePass`. `Ready=False` and phase `Degraded` agree with design 03; only the reason differs.

**Note:** The route keeps naming the active revision; the report is that its ClusterIP is gone.

### `AuthAbandonWaiting`

**Conditions:** `Degraded=True`, `PolicyApplyIncomplete=True`, `Ready=False`

**Constant:** `ReasonAuthAbandonWaiting` (`internal/controller/authtxn.go:926`)

> ReasonAuthAbandonWaiting is PolicyApplyIncomplete's reason while an abandoned transaction's policy delete has returned and the object is still held by a finalizer: status keeps the transaction until it is gone.

**Set at:**

- `internal/controller/agent_controller.go:1153` in `withholdReady()` — from `w.reason`, one of the 12 reasons that field can hold
- `internal/controller/authtxn.go:1052` in `abandonWaiting()` — constant at the call site
- `internal/controller/agent_controller.go:1151` in `withholdReady()` — from `w.reason`, one of the 12 reasons that field can hold

**Referenced by a test:** `test/envtest/authabandonlive_test.go`, `test/envtest/authlockreview_test.go`, `test/envtest/authreview3_test.go`

**State:** A transaction whose target no longer matches the spec was abandoned, and the route or policy delete it issued has returned while the object is still held by another controller's finalizer.

**What the operator does:** Keeps the abandoned transaction in the slot, sets `PolicyApplyIncomplete=True`, withholds `Ready` if nothing else has, and requeues after 30 seconds.

**Traffic:** **depends on the arm** — this reason is raised from more than one state, and traffic stops in some of them. The note below says which.

**Note:** Withdrawn on the `Create` arm: the route's `backendRefs` are stripped and the route deleted BEFORE this reason is raised. Not withdrawn on the `Lock`'s policy-delete arm, which touches no route.

### `AuthEnforcementPending`

**Conditions:** `Degraded=True`, `Ready=False`

**Constant:** `ReasonAuthEnforcementPending` (`internal/controller/authtxn.go:106`)

> Ready, while a `Create` is short of `Served` and before its deadline.

**Set at:**

- `internal/controller/agent_controller.go:1153` in `withholdReady()` — from `w.reason`, one of the 12 reasons that field can hold
- `internal/controller/agent_controller.go:1151` in `withholdReady()` — from `w.reason`, one of the 12 reasons that field can hold

**Referenced by a test:** `test/envtest/authcheck_test.go`, `test/envtest/authcreate_test.go`

**State:** A `Create` is short of `Served` and still before its deadline, with nothing else withholding `Ready`. It is raised only on the arm where the route is not yet published.

**What the operator does:** Carries `Ready=False`. Phase is `Pending` for an Agent that never served, and `Degraded` where a served Agent's route is being re-created.

**Traffic:** **withdrawn** — requests stop reaching the agent.

**Note:** It is set only while the route is PREPARED WITH NO `backendRefs` — written, matched, and sending nothing anywhere. That is the compiler's whole point: a new API-key Agent's route is published only after an anonymous request through it gets `401`.

### `AuthEnforcementUnverified`

**Conditions:** `Degraded=True`, `PolicyApplyIncomplete=True`, `Ready=False`

**Constant:** `ReasonAuthEnforcementUnverified` (`internal/controller/authtxn.go:78`)

> PolicyApplyIncomplete (§3.3.3, §5).

**Set at:**

- `internal/controller/agent_controller.go:1153` in `withholdReady()` — from `w.reason`, one of the 12 reasons that field can hold
- `internal/controller/authtxn.go:1487` in `runCreate()` — constant at the call site
- `internal/controller/agent_controller.go:1151` in `withholdReady()` — from `w.reason`, one of the 12 reasons that field can hold

**Referenced by a test:** `internal/controller/authserved_unit_test.go`, `test/envtest/authabove_test.go`, `test/envtest/authcreate_test.go`, `test/envtest/authlock_test.go`, `test/envtest/authreview3_test.go`

**State:** A `Create` whose deadline has passed, or one that saw a genuine NACK from the Gateway naming its `<agent>-auth`.

**What the operator does:** Sets `PolicyApplyIncomplete=True` and withholds `Ready` if nothing else has. The transaction goes on working and goes on requeuing; it is not abandoned.

**Traffic:** **depends on the arm** — this reason is raised from more than one state, and traffic stops in some of them. The note below says which.

**Note:** Withdrawn while the transaction is short of `Publishing` — the route stays prepared with no `backendRefs`. Not withdrawn once it has published, where `Publishing` has already written them.

### `AuthInputAbsent`

**Conditions:** `Degraded=True`, `PolicyCompileFailed=True`, `Ready=False`

**Constant:** `ReasonAuthInputAbsent` (`internal/controller/authtxn.go:74`)

> PolicyCompileFailed (§3.3.1).

**Set at:**

- `internal/controller/agent_controller.go:1153` in `withholdReady()` — from `w.reason`, one of the 12 reasons that field can hold
- `internal/controller/authtxn.go:797` in `authStep()` — from `fails[0].reason`, one of the 3 reasons that field can hold
- `internal/controller/authtxn.go:826` in `authStep()` — from `fails[0].reason`, one of the 3 reasons that field can hold
- `internal/controller/agent_controller.go:1151` in `withholdReady()` — from `w.reason`, one of the 12 reasons that field can hold

**Referenced by a test:** `internal/controller/authtxn_test.go`, `internal/controller/conditions_test.go`, `test/envtest/authcreate_test.go`, `test/envtest/authlock_test.go`, `test/envtest/authrecreate_test.go`, `test/envtest/authreview3_test.go`

**State:** Compiling `spec.expose.a2a.auth` failed — `oauth`, which no build here compiles, is the ordinary cause.

**What the operator does:** Sets `PolicyCompileFailed=True` and withholds `Ready`. NO TRANSACTION IS ENTERED. A served Agent keeps the last `-auth` that worked.

**Traffic:** **depends on the arm** — this reason is raised from more than one state, and traffic stops in some of them. The note below says which.

**Note:** Not withdrawn for a served Agent: its route goes on serving under the `-auth` it already has (design 03 §3.3.1, I1). For an Agent that never served, no route is published and its own unpublished routes are collected — there was never traffic to withdraw.

### `AuthInputUncompilable`

**Conditions:** `Progressing=True`

**Constant:** none — written as a string literal at the call site.

**Set at:**

- `internal/controller/agent_controller.go:916` in `Reconcile()` — constant at the call site

**Referenced by a test:** **no — no test file in this repository names it.** Nothing here fails if it changes or stops being set.

**State:** The current spec's `-auth` input does not compile, an earlier revision is active, and its digest differs from the digest this spec computes to, so the new revision cannot be promoted.

**What the operator does:** Records the candidate revision, holds the promotion, sets phase `Held`, and leaves `Ready=True` with reason `Available` because the agent is still serving. `PolicyCompileFailed` carries what to change.

**Traffic:** **not withdrawn** — the route goes on serving; only status changes.

**Note:** `status.activeRevision` is untouched, so the route keeps the `-auth` it was last served with and the backend it already names (design 03 §3.3.1, I1).

### `AuthLockPending`

**Conditions:** `GovernanceSkipped=True`

**Constant:** `ReasonAuthLockPending` (`internal/controller/authtxn.go:112`)

**Set at:**

- `internal/controller/authtxn.go:2061` in `runLock()` — constant at the call site
- `internal/controller/httproute.go:725` in `assessGovernance()` — constant at the call site

**Referenced by a test:** `test/e2e/auth_helpers_test.go`, `test/envtest/authabove_test.go`, `test/envtest/authlock_test.go`, `test/envtest/authlockreview_test.go`, `test/envtest/authreview4_test.go`

**State:** A `Lock` is in the slot that is not a re-creation: a served `auth: none` Agent edited to `apikey` (J2), or a refused `Adopt` being locked (K2).

**What the operator does:** Sets `GovernanceSkipped=True`. The `Lock` re-asserts the route published on `status.activeRevision`, writes `<agent>-auth` onto it, and probes.

**Traffic:** **not withdrawn** — the route goes on serving; only status changes.

**Note:** The route keeps its `backendRefs` throughout the lock. This is the whole design of J2: the Agent goes on answering while its authentication is put in place underneath it.

### `AuthLockUnverified`

**Conditions:** `Degraded=True`, `PolicyApplyIncomplete=True`, `Ready=False`

**Constant:** `ReasonAuthLockUnverified` (`internal/controller/authtxn.go:79`)

**Set at:**

- `internal/controller/agent_controller.go:1153` in `withholdReady()` — from `w.reason`, one of the 12 reasons that field can hold
- `internal/controller/authtxn.go:2066` in `runLock()` — constant at the call site
- `internal/controller/httproute.go:727` in `assessGovernance()` — constant at the call site
- `internal/controller/agent_controller.go:1151` in `withholdReady()` — from `w.reason`, one of the 12 reasons that field can hold

**Referenced by a test:** `internal/controller/authserved_unit_test.go`, `test/conformance/slice_cluster_test.go`, `test/envtest/authabove_test.go`, `test/envtest/authlock_test.go`, `test/envtest/authlockrace_test.go`, `test/envtest/authlockreview_test.go`, `test/envtest/authreview4_test.go`

**State:** A `Lock` is past its deadline, or it saw a NACK. The policy has been written and the `401` that would prove it has not been credited.

**What the operator does:** Sets `PolicyApplyIncomplete=True`, `Ready=False` and phase `Degraded`. The `Lock` keeps working.

**Traffic:** **not withdrawn** — the route goes on serving; only status changes.

**Note:** The route keeps serving, OPEN, exactly as before the edit. The Agent is degraded because its declared authentication is not proved, not because it stopped answering.

### `AuthPolicyNotAttached`

**Conditions:** `Degraded=True`, `GovernanceSkipped=True`, `PolicyApplyIncomplete=True`, `Ready=False`

**Constant:** `ReasonAuthPolicyNotAttached` (`internal/controller/authtxn.go:104`)

**Set at:**

- `internal/controller/agent_controller.go:1153` in `withholdReady()` — from `w.reason`, one of the 12 reasons that field can hold
- `internal/controller/authserved.go:809` in `appendGovernance()` — from the local `reason`, which folds to this one reason
- `internal/controller/authtxn.go:605` in `raiseIncomplete()` — from the local `reason`, one of 8 reasons it folds to
- `internal/controller/authtxn.go:607` in `raiseIncomplete()` — from the local `reason`, one of 8 reasons it folds to
- `internal/controller/agent_controller.go:1151` in `withholdReady()` — from `w.reason`, one of the 12 reasons that field can hold

**Referenced by a test:** `internal/controller/authserved_unit_test.go`, `test/conformance/ancestor.go`, `test/conformance/slice_attach_cluster_test.go`, `test/envtest/authserved_test.go`, `test/envtest/service_reads_test.go`, `test/envtest/service_test.go`

**State:** A served `<agent>-auth` exists, carries the Agent's UID and renders to the recorded `appliedDigest`, and the Gateway reports its tuple broken at the policy's current generation. "Broken" is four different answers, and since design 03 A83 the message says which: the policy rejected outright (`Accepted=False`); accepted but not in whole (`Accepted=True` with a reason other than `Valid`); attached to nothing (`Attached=False`); or only the synthetic `StatusSummary` ancestor present.

**What the operator does:** Sets `PolicyApplyIncomplete=True` and `GovernanceSkipped=True`, `Ready=False`, phase `Degraded`, and records the claim on `status.auth.policyUnattached` so it is re-asserted on passes that learn nothing new.

**Traffic:** **not withdrawn** — the route goes on serving; only status changes.

**Code and design disagree:** The REASON still names non-attachment for a clause where the Gateway says the opposite, and only the message says otherwise — as does the `status.auth.policyUnattached` field name. And a policy carrying the synthetic ancestor beside a real one reporting `Attached=True` still takes the non-attachment lead, which design 03 records as owed. And on a route read UNKNOWN with no route claim standing, the hedged lead says "PolicyApplyIncomplete names the route's own reading first" while being that condition's whole message, which carries no route reading — permanently so on a cluster whose agentgateway controller is renamed. Design 03 records it as owed (§8.1 item 11, A84).

**Note:** Nothing is withdrawn, deleted or rewritten: this is the fail-open half, ANNOUNCED AND NOT CLOSED. Since design 03 A83 the MESSAGE says which of the four answers the Gateway gave, and the partly-valid one — the only shape a cluster measurement on agentgateway 1.5.0 has reached with a byte-unchanged policy, where the route was still answering `401` — no longer claims the policy is unattached or that a credential may not be required. It says instead that the judgement reads the Gateway's report, issues no request, and so did not check. The REASON does not branch: one string covers all four answers.

**State:** An object at a desired revision's name — its Deployment or its Service — does not carry this Agent's UID in its `assayd.dev/agent-uid` label: the label is absent, which is the commonest plant, or it names another Agent. On the Service path this is reached only by an object whose UID `status.revisionServices` does not record; the one it records is the operator's own whatever its labels say.

**What the operator does:** Refuses it and never rewrites or deletes it. Sets `RevisionHashCollision=True` with this reason, `Ready=False` and `Degraded=True` under `RevisionHashCollision`, phase `Degraded`, and returns before the gateway step. On the Service path it re-checks after `RefusedServiceRecheck` (one minute). On the workload path the pass requests no requeue; an event on a Deployment the watch maps to this Agent can still enqueue it, but a refused object usually carries none of the labels that mapping reads.

**Traffic:** **not withdrawn** — the route goes on serving; only status changes.

**Note:** Before A77 this ground reported `DigestMismatch`.

### `RevisionServiceNotRecorded`

**Conditions:** `Degraded=True`, `Ready=False`

**Constant:** none — written as a string literal at the call site.

- `internal/controller/agent_controller.go:686` in `Reconcile()` — from the local `shape.reason(…)`, one of 2 reasons it folds to

**Referenced by a test:** `test/envtest/service_record_test.go`

**State:** A Service at the desired revision's name is headless — `spec.clusterIP: None`, which no Update can repair — and its UID is not the one `status.revisionServices` records for that revision and digest. There is no record: an Agent created before the record, whose Service went headless before it was adopted; or the record of the operator's own create was lost — its dedicated status write and the pass's final status write both failed, or the process died between the create and them — before the object went headless. Or the record names a different object: the operator's Service was deleted and another put at the name, or the operator's own replacement lost its record in the same way. The object passed provenance, so it is not a collision; the operator cannot establish that it created or adopted it, whatever its labels and annotations say.

**What the operator does:** Never deletes it. Sets `Ready=False` and `Degraded=True` with this reason and phase `Degraded`, carries design 03's `PolicyApplyIncomplete` and `PolicyCompileFailed`, returns before the gateway step, and re-checks after `RefusedServiceRecheck` (one minute). The message names the recorded UID and the object's. It stands until a human deletes the object, after which the operator creates its own and records it, or repairs it in place back to addressable, after which the next pass converges it and, if there is no record at that revision and digest, adopts it.

**Traffic:** **not withdrawn** — the route goes on serving; only status changes.

**Note:** If the revision is active, its route still names this object.

### `RevisionServiceReplaceFailed`

**Conditions:** `Degraded=True`, `Ready=False`

**Constant:** none — written as a string literal at the call site.

**Set at:**

- `internal/controller/agent_controller.go:658` in `Reconcile()` — constant at the call site
- `internal/controller/agent_controller.go:656` in `Reconcile()` — constant at the call site

**Referenced by a test:** **no — no test file in this repository names it.** Nothing here fails if it changes or stops being set.

**State:** The operator's own revision Service — the object whose UID `status.revisionServices` records — is headless and cannot be repaired in place, and its delete-and-recreate did not complete. The message names the stage: the dry-run create of the replacement was refused ("would not be admitted"), which is the likeliest and deletes nothing; the delete was refused ("could not be deleted"), by a lost UID precondition because the object at the name is no longer the recorded one, or by any other API error; the object had already gone ("vanished before it could be replaced"); the recreate failed after the delete ("could not be recreated after it was deleted"); or the replacement was stored with no ClusterIP ("was recreated with no ClusterIP"), as a mutating webhook forcing `clusterIP: None` would do.

**What the operator does:** Sets `Ready=False` and `Degraded=True` with this reason and phase `Degraded`, carries design 03's `PolicyApplyIncomplete` and `PolicyCompileFailed`, writes status, returns before the gateway step, and re-checks after `RefusedServiceRecheck` (one minute). It never reports success, so the revision is not promoted over whatever holds the name.

**Traffic:** **not withdrawn** — the route goes on serving; only status changes.

**Note:** The route names the Service by name, so what it reaches depends on the stage. After a refused dry-run or a refused delete, the object the operator read is still there, unless the precondition was lost, in which case somebody else's object is. After a vanished object or a failed recreate, the name may hold nothing or an object someone else created. After a headless replacement, it holds the operator's new, recorded object, which has no ClusterIP.

**State:** The operator's live `get` of the desired revision's Service was answered with a status error that is neither NotFound nor transient — most often Forbidden or Unauthorized, meaning the operator's own credentials may not read services. The Service is not at fault. The chart's operator ClusterRole grants the verb cluster-wide.

**What the operator does:** Writes nothing to the Service. Sets `Ready=False` and `Degraded=True` with this reason and phase `Degraded`, carries design 03's `PolicyApplyIncomplete` and `PolicyCompileFailed`, returns before the gateway step, and re-checks after `RefusedServiceRecheck` (one minute). For a Forbidden or Unauthorized the message names the missing permission; it never tells the reader to delete anything. A transient read error raises nothing and is retried with backoff.

**Traffic:** **not withdrawn** — the route goes on serving; only status changes.

**State:** Any non-transient failure out of the gateway step that is not one of the typed gateway errors — a route write the API server refused, a serving Service or port that could not be read, a route name collision. It is the fallback reason, written as a literal with no constant.

**What the operator does:** Raises `PolicyApplyIncomplete` — though only where this pass asserted nothing stronger, because the literal is not in the ranking and an unranked write error never displaces a standing report. Sets `Ready=False`, and `Degraded` with phase `Degraded` for an Agent that was serving or `Pending` for a `Create` that never served. Returns the error so the queue retries.

**Traffic:** **not established.** The code was read and the answer was not settled; this page will not guess.

**Note:** It names a write that did NOT land, so the route keeps whatever state it already had, and whether that state was serving depends on which write failed. Nothing on this path strips or deletes a route. The reference will not collapse that into a yes or a no.

### `ServiceRejected`

**Conditions:** `Degraded=True`, `Ready=False`

**Constant:** none — written as a string literal at the call site.

**Set at:**

- `internal/controller/agent_controller.go:752` in `Reconcile()` — constant at the call site
- `internal/controller/agent_controller.go:751` in `Reconcile()` — constant at the call site

**Referenced by a test:** `test/envtest/service_reads_test.go`, `test/envtest/service_test.go`

**State:** The API server answered this operator's create or update of a revision's Service with a status error that is not on the transient list — Conflict, NotFound, AlreadyExists, ServerTimeout, Timeout, TooManyRequests, InternalError, ServiceUnavailable and UnexpectedServerError are excluded, and a transport failure that carries no status is retried unreported. That is any other status: an Invalid render or repair, a Forbidden from an admission policy or webhook over `services`, and equally an RBAC Forbidden or an Unauthorized on the write. A refused READ of the Service is not this reason; it is `RevisionServiceUnreadable`.

**What the operator does:** Sets `Ready=False`, `Degraded=True` and phase `Degraded`, carries design 03's `PolicyApplyIncomplete` and `PolicyCompileFailed`, writes status, returns before the gateway step, and re-checks after `RefusedServiceRecheck` (one minute). The message says which write was refused: on a create, that there is no object to delete and to look for an admission policy or webhook over services; on an update, to fix or exempt the policy and then delete the Service so the operator recreates it.

**Traffic:** **not withdrawn** — the route goes on serving; only status changes.

**Note:** The remedy assumes an admission policy. For an RBAC refusal of the write it names the wrong thing to fix, and the message does not tell the two apart, since both arrive as Forbidden.

### `ServingRouteNotAccepted`

**Conditions:** `Degraded=True`, `PolicyApplyIncomplete=True`, `Ready=False`

**Constant:** `ReasonServingRouteNotAccepted` (`internal/controller/authtxn.go:103`)

> A80's two, for a served Agent with no transaction in the slot or a refused Adopt in it: the assayd Gateway reports the serving route refused, and it reports §3.3.2's tuple for the served &lt;agent&gt;-auth BROKEN. AuthPolicyNotAttached is a GovernanceSkipped reason too.  AuthPolicyNotAttached's NAME is narrower than what it covers, and that is a decision rather than an oversight: since A83 the reason also carries the clause in which the Gateway accepted the policy only in part and reported it ATTACHED. The human kept (B1)'s condition set on 2026-09-23 and D5(b) is decided as no, because the claim store on status.auth is one boolean per half and carries no clause, so a per-clause reason could not be re-asserted on a pass that re-derives nothing. The MESSAGE names what the Gateway actually said (§5, §9 D5).

**Set at:**

- `internal/controller/agent_controller.go:1153` in `withholdReady()` — from `w.reason`, one of the 12 reasons that field can hold
- `internal/controller/authtxn.go:605` in `raiseIncomplete()` — from the local `reason`, one of 8 reasons it folds to
- `internal/controller/authtxn.go:607` in `raiseIncomplete()` — from the local `reason`, one of 8 reasons it folds to
- `internal/controller/agent_controller.go:1151` in `withholdReady()` — from `w.reason`, one of the 12 reasons that field can hold

**Referenced by a test:** `internal/controller/authserved_unit_test.go`, `test/envtest/authserved_test.go`, `test/envtest/service_precedence_test.go`

**State:** On a pass of a SERVED Agent with no transaction in the slot, or a refused `Adopt` in it, the assayd Gateway's own entry for this route — matched on both `parentRef` and controller name — reports `Accepted=False` or `ResolvedRefs=False` AT THE ROUTE'S CURRENT GENERATION.

**What the operator does:** Sets `PolicyApplyIncomplete=True`, `Ready=False` and phase `Degraded`, leaves `GovernanceSkipped` where it was with a note, and records the claim on `status.auth.routeRefused` so it is re-asserted on passes that learn nothing new.

**Traffic:** **not withdrawn** — the route goes on serving; only status changes.

**Note:** Explicitly not withdrawn: the route is left alone and its `backendRefs` are not stripped. Anything that is not an explicit failure at the current generation is treated as unknown — it raises nothing and clears nothing — because every route write bumps the generation and the Gateway's report lags it.

### `TeardownWaiting`

**Conditions:** `Ready=False`

**Constant:** `ReasonTeardownWaiting` (`internal/controller/gatewaywiring.go:75`)

> ReasonTeardownWaiting is Ready=False on an Agent being deleted whose teardown is waiting for a delete that has not completed. The message names the object and the finalizers holding it, because nothing else says why the Agent is still Terminating (NFR-8).

**Set at:**

- `internal/controller/gatewaywiring.go:174` in `reportTeardownWaiting()` — constant at the call site

**Referenced by a test:** `test/envtest/gatewaywiring_test.go`

**State:** The Agent is being deleted with the gateway enabled, and the serving route or the `-auth` policy has been sent a delete that has not completed — another controller's finalizer is holding it.

**What the operator does:** Writes `Ready=False` alone and leaves every other condition as it is, then requeues after 30 seconds. Teardown goes no further: the workload, the Service and the revision material are not deleted while either gateway delete is pending.

**Traffic:** **withdrawn** — requests stop reaching the agent.

**Note:** The route's delete has already been issued; it is still present only because a finalizer holds it. Routes are deleted before policies, so the reverse order cannot leave a published route with no authentication.

**Conditions:** `RevisionHashCollision=True`

**Constant:** none — written as a string literal at the call site.

**State:** An object at a desired revision's name — its Deployment or its Service — carries this Agent's UID label but no revision-digest stamp, and `status` vouches for no such revision: it is neither the active nor the candidate revision at this digest. **Traffic:** **not withdrawn** — the route goes on serving; only status changes.

**Note:** Until round three of design 02 A77's review this reason also named a headless Service the operator would not delete. That is `RevisionServiceNotRecorded` now, because the object refused there may carry a stamp.

## Reasons no test in this repository names

18 of the 71 reasons the operator can set are named by no test file
anywhere under `internal/`, `api/` or `test/`. Each is a string this operator will put on a user's
object, and no test in this repository fails if it changes, stops being set, or is set for the
wrong state. That is not a claim that the BEHAVIOUR is untested — a test can exercise a path and
assert only its phase — it is the narrower and exact claim that the reason string itself is
unpinned.

## Honesty notes

**How each reason was resolved.** A call site passes its reason as a constant, a struct field or a
local, and the three are not equally strong:

| Resolution | Sites | What it means |
|---|---|---|
| `constant` | 62 | A string literal or a `Reason*` constant at the call site. Exact. |
| `field` | 6 | A struct field (`failure.reason` and its siblings). The listed reasons are every constant written into that field, narrowed to the function that built the value where the generator could follow it. One pass sets ONE of them; which one is not claimed. |
| `local` | 17 | A local whose assignments — and, one hop, the in-package function they call — all fold to constants. |
| `carried` | 6 | The reason is read back off a condition an earlier pass stored. It introduces no new reason and appears in no reason's site list. |
| `unresolved` | 0 | The generator could not fold the expression. |

**Every call site resolved.** No condition write in `internal/controller` has a reason this page could not fold, so the list above is the whole vocabulary this build can set.

**Traffic not established.** For 1 reason(s) the question "is traffic withdrawn?" was not settled
from the code, and the page says `unknown` rather than guessing:

- [`RouteApplyFailed`](#routeapplyfailed)

**Where the code and a design disagree.** 6 reason(s) carry a recorded disagreement, quoted in
their own section above. This page reports them; it does not settle them.

- [`ActiveRevisionServiceUnaddressable`](#activerevisionserviceunaddressable)
- [`AuthPolicyNotAttached`](#authpolicynotattached)
- [`MaterialInvalid`](#materialinvalid)
- [`MaterialUnavailable`](#materialunavailable)
- [`NoGatesDeclared`](#nogatesdeclared)
- [`RevisionMaterialUnavailable`](#revisionmaterialunavailable)

**Conditions re-asserted rather than decided.** 8 call site(s) re-assert a condition an EARLIER pass stored, verbatim — the mechanism that keeps a standing report from being retracted by a pass that learned nothing new. They introduce no reason of their own, so they appear in no reason's site list above, and the reason they carry is whichever one was stored.

**Every reason set is closed.** Each struct reason field the page reads had all of its writes folded, so a `field` row lists every reason that field can hold.

**Coverage of the test reference scan.** 53 of 71 reasons are named by at least one test file. The scan matches the reason string or its `Reason*` identifier on a word boundary, across every `_test.go` under `internal/` and `api/` and every Go file under `test/`. `internal/refgen` is excluded: its tests name reasons to check that the GENERATOR resolves them, and counting those would let this page shrink its own unpinned list.
